# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated from the settings table in internal/infra/config by `task generate`. Do not edit. -->

Flagnetic is configured with environment variables and, optionally, a YAML file named by `FLAGNETIC_CONFIG_FILE`. Each setting is read from its environment variable when that is set, even to the empty string; otherwise from the file; otherwise it takes its default. An empty value means the default, except where a setting says it switches something off.

The file is a mapping from the keys in the File key column to single values:

```yaml
database_url: postgres://flagnetic@db:5432/flagnetic?sslmode=require
listen_addr: ":8080"
log_format: text
```

A file key that is not listed here, a value that is not a single value, and a value that does not parse are refused when the server starts, with exit code 2 and a message naming the setting.

Durations are written as a number and a unit: `500ms`, `15s`, `2m`.

| Variable | File key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | `database_url` | required | PostgreSQL connection string, as a URL or as keyword/value pairs. PostgreSQL 16 or newer. What it leaves out is taken from the standard PostgreSQL variables, such as `PGPASSWORD`, so the password need not be in it. Example: `postgres://flagnetic@db:5432/flagnetic?sslmode=require`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_SECRET_KEY` | `secret_key` | required by `serve` | The instance's secret key: stored secrets are sealed under it, sessions are signed with it. Keep it for the life of the instance: on its first start the instance stores a canary sealed under the key, and `serve` refuses to start under a key that does not open it. At least 32 bytes: use a long random value, such as the output of `openssl rand -base64 32`. Example: `q3S0k1p2Rk7Jt0E5m9xV8bYcN4wZ6hL2aU1dG7fH0eI=`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_BASE_URL` | `base_url` | — | The public URL the console is reached at, such as the address of the reverse proxy in front. Its scheme decides whether the session cookie is `Secure`, and its origin is trusted for requests signed in through the console even when the proxy rewrites `Host`. Invitation links start with it. When unset, the scheme and origin of each request are used. Auth providers need it: a provider's redirect URI, which the identity provider is told, is built from it, so creating, editing or enabling one is refused with `base_url_required` while it is unset. Example: `https://flags.example.com`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_INSECURE_COOKIES` | `insecure_cookies` | `false` | Send the session cookie without `Secure` over plain HTTP on a host other than localhost, for a trial without TLS. On localhost the cookie works over plain HTTP without it. Never set it where the console is reached over a network you do not trust. Example: `true`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_PASSWORD_HASH_CONCURRENCY` | `password_hash_concurrency` | `4` | How many passwords one replica hashes or verifies at once. Each takes 64 MiB of memory for about a tenth of a second, so the bound keeps a burst of sign-ins from exhausting the replica. A sign-in that waits more than 2 seconds for a slot is answered 503 `busy` with `Retry-After`. Example: `8`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_DEFAULT_LOCALE` | `default_locale` | `en` | The console's language when the member has not chosen one and the browser asks for none the console offers: `en` (English) or `ru` (Russian). Example: `ru`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_TEST_CLOCK_FILE` | — | — | Test only: a file holding a duration, such as `25h`, that moves the server's clock ahead, read again on every use. Accepted only by the end-to-end test harness, listening on loopback; refused anywhere else. Environment only. Example: `/tmp/flagnetic-clock-offset`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_CONFIG_FILE` | — | — | YAML file of settings, keyed by the names in the File key column. Environment only. Example: `/etc/flagnetic/flagnetic.yaml`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_LISTEN_ADDR` | `listen_addr` | `:8080` | Address of the public listener: the APIs, the console, `/healthz` and `/readyz`. Example: `:8080`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_METRICS_LISTEN_ADDR` | `metrics_listen_addr` | `:9090` | Address of the metrics listener, which serves Prometheus metrics on `/metrics` and nothing else. Keep it off the internet. Set it empty to switch metrics off and open no port. Example: `127.0.0.1:9090`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_AUTO_MIGRATE` | `auto_migrate` | `true` | Whether `serve` applies pending migrations on start. Set it to false when migrations run as a job (`flagnetic migrate`). Example: `false`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_DB_MAX_CONNS` | `db_max_conns` | `10` | Size of the PostgreSQL connection pool of one replica. When unset, `pool_max_conns` in `DATABASE_URL` applies if present; when both are set, this wins and a notice is logged. Unit: connections. Example: `25`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN` | `shutdown_drain` | `5s` | How long a replica told to stop keeps serving while `/readyz` answers 503, so load balancers route away from it before it stops accepting requests. `0` skips the drain. Unit: duration. Example: `5s`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_SHUTDOWN_GRACE` | `shutdown_grace` | `15s` | How long in-flight requests may run once the drain is over and the replica stops accepting new ones; then they are cancelled. Unit: duration. Example: `15s`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_LOG_LEVEL` | `log_level` | `info` | Lowest level logged: debug, info, warn or error. Example: `debug`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_LOG_FORMAT` | `log_format` | `json` | Format of the log written to standard error: json, one object per line, or text. Example: `text`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | `trusted_proxies` | — | Comma-separated CIDR prefixes or single addresses of the reverse proxies in front of the server. Their `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` headers are believed, so the client's address and scheme are the real client's; from any other peer the headers are ignored, so a client cannot choose the address it is seen with. Example: `10.0.0.0/8,192.168.1.10`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_HTTP_READ_HEADER_TIMEOUT` | `http_read_header_timeout` | `10s` | How long a client may take to send a request's headers on the public listener. Unit: duration. Example: `10s`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_HTTP_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | `http_idle_timeout` | `120s` | How long a keep-alive connection may stay idle before the server closes it. Unit: duration. Example: `120s`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_HTTP_BODY_READ_TIMEOUT` | `http_body_read_timeout` | `30s` | How long a client may take to send a request's body; a body still arriving then is answered 408. Long-lived streams are excepted. Unit: duration. Example: `30s`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_HTTP_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `http_max_body_bytes` | `1048576` | Largest request body accepted, unless a route declares a larger limit of its own; a larger body is answered 413. Unit: bytes. Example: `1048576`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_EVENTS_RETENTION_DAYS` | `events_retention_days` | `30` | The window of the raw events SDKs post. An event whose time is older, after the batch's clock-skew shift, is rejected `out_of_window`. Raw events are kept as long: each day is dropped once it is wholly older. An event ID is recognised as a retry and the event stored once for a year, or the window plus a day when that is longer, so it outlives the raw events. Unit: days. Example: `30`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_EVENTS_PARTITIONS_AHEAD` | `events_partitions_ahead` | `3` | How many days after today the raw event tables' daily partitions are created ahead of time, so that events received after midnight never wait for one. Unit: days. Example: `3`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_SDK_INVENTORY_RETENTION_DAYS` | `sdk_inventory_retention_days` | `90` | How long an environment's SDK inventory keeps an SDK after it was last seen. An SDK seen again afterwards appears again, with a new first-seen time. Unit: days. Example: `90`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP` | `webhook_allow_http` | `false` | Accept webhook subscriptions and webhook sinks whose target is plain `http`, which sends events and their signatures unencrypted. Without it such a target is refused `insecure_url`. Meant for a receiver on the same host or a trusted network. Example: `true`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` | `webhook_allow_private_networks` | `false` | Accept webhook targets that resolve to loopback, private, link-local, unspecified or multicast addresses. Without it such a target is refused `private_network_target` when a subscription or a webhook sink is written, so that whoever manages webhooks or sinks cannot reach the network the instance runs in. ClickHouse and object storage sinks may reach private networks regardless, and never a link-local address. Example: `true`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_WEBHOOK_TICK` | `webhook_tick` | `5s` | How often a replica turns new events into webhook deliveries and sends the deliveries that are due. An event reaches a receiver about this long after its change at the earliest. Unit: duration. Example: `5s`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_WEBHOOK_SECRET_OVERLAP` | `webhook_secret_overlap` | `24h` | How long the secret a rotation replaced, a webhook subscription's or a webhook sink's, keeps signing beside the new one, so a receiver can take the new secret without refusing a single event. Unit: duration. Example: `24h`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_SCHEDULE_MIN_LEAD` | `schedule_min_lead` | `60s` | How far ahead a change request's apply time must be at least when it is set; a sooner time is refused `invalid_change_request`. Unit: duration. Example: `5m`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_SCHEDULE_TICK` | `schedule_tick` | `10s` | How often every replica looks for approved change requests whose apply time has come and applies them; a change request is applied at most this long after its time, or later when no replica was running. Unit: duration. Example: `10s`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_SCHEDULE_MAX_FAILURES` | `schedule_max_failures` | `5` | How many scheduled applications of a change request may fail in a row before the scheduler stops trying it and records `change_request.schedule_failed`. Unit: attempts. Example: `5`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_AUDIT_EXPORT_MAX_ENTRIES` | `audit_export_max_entries` | `100000` | The most entries one download of the audit log may hold. A download whose filters match more is refused `export_too_large` before anything is sent; narrowing it by time brings it under. Unit: entries. Example: `100000`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_DIGEST_WEEKDAY` | `digest_weekday` | `monday` | The weekday, in UTC, on which the stale-flag digest (`report.stale_flags`) is sent to each project's webhook subscribers, in English, in any case. A digest not sent within the hour of its slot because no replica was running is skipped, not sent late. Unit: weekday. Example: `friday`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_DIGEST_HOUR` | `digest_hour` | `8` | The hour of the day, in UTC, at which the stale-flag digest is sent on its weekday; it is sent at the first minute of that hour that a replica runs. Unit: hour, 0 to 23. Example: `14`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_CLIENT_EVALUATE` | `rate_limit_client_evaluate` | `120` | Remote evaluations a client key may ask of one replica per minute, counted per key and client IP, an IPv6 client by its /64. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: requests per minute. Example: `120`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_CLIENT_EVENTS` | `rate_limit_client_events` | `60` | Event batches a client key may post to one replica per minute, counted per key and client IP, an IPv6 client by its /64. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: requests per minute. Example: `60`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_CLIENT_STREAM_CONNECTS` | `rate_limit_client_stream_connects` | `30` | Ruleset streams a client key may open on one replica per minute, counted per key and client IP, an IPv6 client by its /64. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: requests per minute. Example: `30`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_CLIENT_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` | `rate_limit_client_concurrent_streams` | `10` | Ruleset streams a client key may hold open on one replica at once, counted per key and client IP, an IPv6 client by its /64. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: streams. Example: `10`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_CLIENT_STREAMS_PER_REPLICA` | `rate_limit_client_streams_per_replica` | `10000` | Ruleset streams all client keys together may hold open on one replica at once, whatever their keys and client IPs, which bounds the connections a public client key can hold the replica to. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: streams. Example: `10000`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_SERVER_RULESET` | `rate_limit_server_ruleset` | `600` | Ruleset downloads a server key may ask of one replica per minute, counted per key. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: requests per minute. Example: `600`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_SERVER_EVALUATE` | `rate_limit_server_evaluate` | `6000` | Remote evaluations a server key may ask of one replica per minute, counted per key. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: requests per minute. Example: `6000`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_SERVER_EVENTS` | `rate_limit_server_events` | `600` | Event batches a server key may post to one replica per minute, counted per key. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: requests per minute. Example: `600`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_SERVER_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` | `rate_limit_server_concurrent_streams` | `1000` | Ruleset streams a server key may hold open on one replica at once, counted per key. A server key's stream connects are not limited per minute. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: streams. Example: `1000`. |
| `FLAGNETIC_RATE_LIMIT_FAILED_AUTHENTICATIONS` | `rate_limit_failed_authentications` | `30` | SDK API requests from one client IP (an IPv6 client by its /64) whose key is malformed or unknown that one replica takes per minute. Past it, an SDK API request from that IP or /64 is answered 429 before its key is looked up, which keeps guessing keys slow, unless the replica already holds its key from an earlier lookup, so the valid keys in use behind a shared address keep working. A revoked or expired key, and a request without a key, are not counted. Each replica counts on its own, so an instance of n replicas lets up to n times as much through. A refused request is answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. `off` switches the limit off. Unit: refusals per minute. Example: `30`. |

One more variable is read by `flagnetic admin bootstrap` and `flagnetic admin create` alone, never by `serve`: `FLAGNETIC_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, the password of the instance admin they create (environment only; when unset, a password is generated and printed once). See [The first instance admin](operations.md#the-first-instance-admin).
